title: Senate Floor Debate
subtitle: S.4522 — Secure Our Schools and Communities Act

metadata.laymanSummary: With bipartisan support, the Senate passed school safety legislation funding threat assessment programs, mental health resources, and physical security upgrades at K-12 schools.

data.billTitle: Secure Our Schools and Communities Act — $12B for threat assessment, mental health, and school physical security

speakers.name: Sen. Roger Wicker
speakers.title: R-MS · Senate Armed Services Chair
speakers.quote: I have grandchildren in public school. This bill does what works: threat assessment teams that identify students in crisis before they act, mental health counselors who can intervene, and hardened entry points that give responders time to react. This is not a gun debate. This is a school safety debate. We can agree on school safety.

speakers.name: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse
speakers.title: D-RI · Senate Judiciary
speakers.quote: School shootings have killed more American students than combat has killed American soldiers in every war since Korea combined. This bill is overdue by twenty years. It is not sufficient — we still need to address how those shooters got their weapons — but it is a critical first step and I am proud to vote for it.

speakers.name: Sen. Rand Paul
speakers.title: R-KY · Senate
speakers.quote: Local school safety is a local decision, funded by local tax dollars, responsive to local communities. When Washington funds school security, Washington sets the standards — and those standards include data collection on students, surveillance systems, and mental health screenings that I would not want conducted on my children without my consent.

data.title: What This Vote Means
data.text: S.4522 passed 65-34 with strong bipartisan support — one of the most cross-partisan gun-related votes in years. The bill appropriates $12 billion over five years for behavioral threat assessment training in all US schools, mental health counselor grants, and physical security upgrades. Unlike the background checks bill, it contains no firearm restrictions, which enabled Republican support.
